title: Brand protection: how to defend against counterfeits and copycats
summary: Bustem founder Oliver Brocato explains how e-commerce brands can defend against counterfeits. Register your IP first, enforce takedowns on platforms rather than litigate, monitor at scale because infringers keep reappearing, tighten the supply chain, and educate customers.

principles.text: Register your IP first. It lets you prove ownership when you find fakes.
principles.quote: Registering your intellectual property is the most elementary step in protecting your brand from counterfeits.

principles.text: Detect infringement early. Speed protects profits, goodwill and market position.
principles.quote: The sooner you detect and stop the violation, the better chance you will have to protect your profits, business or product’s goodwill, and overall market position.

principles.text: Prefer platform takedowns over lawsuits when the goal is fast removal. Litigation is slow, costly and uncertain.
principles.quote: Going through litigation is time-consuming and expensive, and there is no guarantee of success.

principles.text: One takedown doesn't end it. Counterfeiters relist across marketplaces and countries, so enforce at scale with technology.
principles.quote: Online brands often play whack-a-mole with counterfeiters because infringers place fake listings on multiple marketplaces across many countries.

principles.text: Close supply chain gaps with strong supplier contracts and traceability so counterfeiters can't exploit them.
principles.quote: Ensure strong supplier contracts and maintain traceability in your supply chain to prevent any form of weakness that counterfeiters could exploit.

principles.text: Educate customers on legitimate channels and how to spot and report fakes to rebuild trust.
principles.quote: Take another step forward at countering counterfeit products by educating your customers on the benefits of opting for legitimate products and the channels where they can find these.
